newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close lower amid poor fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close lower amid poor fundamentals.

text.p: Locals sold stocks and took profits as they believed market fundamentals remain poor, and drove the index to a slightly lower close on Thursday, brokers said.

"Local investors decided to sell in the afternoon as they think that the market fundamentals stayed unchanged. Central bank currency controls which were announced earlier this week caused foreigners to stay away from the market," said a broker at a foreign brokerage.
The composite SET index ended 1.64 points lower at 519.76 on 3.2 billion baht turnover.
Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia said he believed local mutual funds continued buying on Thursday but not aggressively as they feared speculator profit-taking.
"Retailers don't want to hold stocks for a long time. Foreigners were still on the sidelines due to the currency control measures," Samart said.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said earlier on Thursday that stock brokers in the local bourse should not be worried about latest currency control measures introduced by the central bank involving stocks trading.
Samart and other brokers said investors expected that the central bank would issue more measures which would benefit listed companies.
"Persistent concerns by foreigners on the baht control plus a lack of fresh news are major factors which will cause the market to continue falling tomorrow" said the broker at the foreign brokerage.

Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list in terms of value, unchanged at 93 baht. Noble Development, which made its debut today, closed at 6.10, down from its IPO price of 16 baht. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
